per_query.name: comma_join_homephone
per_query.sql: SELECT HomePhone, OrderID FROM Employees, Orders WHERE Employees.EmployeeID = Orders.EmployeeID
per_query.description: Classic comma-join; HomePhone has no table prefix and two tables are in scope.

per_query.name: comma_join_birthdate
per_query.sql: SELECT BirthDate, City FROM Employees, Orders WHERE Employees.EmployeeID = Orders.EmployeeID
per_query.description: Comma-join; BirthDate unqualified.

per_query.name: comma_join_unitprice
per_query.sql: SELECT UnitPrice, ProductName FROM Products, Categories WHERE Products.CategoryID = Categories.CategoryID
per_query.description: Comma-join; UnitPrice (commercial pricing) unqualified.

per_query.name: comma_join_freight
per_query.sql: SELECT Freight, ShipCity FROM Orders, Customers WHERE Orders.CustomerID = Customers.CustomerID
per_query.description: Comma-join; Freight (shipping cost) unqualified.

per_query.name: three_table_comma_join_two_sensitive
per_query.sql: SELECT HomePhone, UnitPrice, OrderID FROM Employees, Orders, "Order Details" WHERE Employees.EmployeeID = Orders.EmployeeID AND Orders.OrderID = "Order Details".OrderID
per_query.description: Three-table comma-join with two unqualified sensitive columns from different tables.

per_query.name: multi_sensitive_single_query
per_query.sql: SELECT HomePhone, BirthDate, OrderID FROM Employees, Orders WHERE Employees.EmployeeID = Orders.EmployeeID
per_query.description: Two unqualified sensitive columns from the SAME table in one comma-join.

per_query.name: aliased_table_unqualified_sensitive_column
per_query.sql: SELECT e.LastName, HomePhone FROM Employees e, Orders o WHERE e.EmployeeID = o.EmployeeID
per_query.description: One column table-aliased (e.LastName), the sensitive one (HomePhone) still unqualified.

per_query.name: unqualified_sensitive_with_join_keyword
per_query.sql: SELECT UnitPrice, ProductName FROM Products p, Suppliers s WHERE p.SupplierID = 1
per_query.description: Comma-join where the join predicate itself doesn't reference the second table -- UnitPrice still ambiguous because two tables are in FROM scope.

per_query.name: fully_qualified_sensitive_control
per_query.sql: SELECT e.HomePhone, o.OrderID FROM Employees e JOIN Orders o ON e.EmployeeID = o.EmployeeID
per_query.description: Control: HomePhone IS table-qualified -- resolves correctly regardless of the fix.

per_query.name: single_table_unqualified_sensitive_control
per_query.sql: SELECT HomePhone, LastName FROM Employees WHERE EmployeeID = 5
per_query.description: Control: only one table in scope, so the extractor's single-table heuristic resolves HomePhone correctly even pre-fix.

per_query.name: comma_join_nonsensitive_control
per_query.sql: SELECT City, Country FROM Customers, Orders WHERE Customers.CustomerID = Orders.CustomerID
per_query.description: Control: unqualified comma-join, but neither column is sensitive -- no leak either way.

per_query.name: comma_join_permitted_sensitive_control
per_query.sql: SELECT UnitPrice, ShipCity FROM Orders, Customers WHERE Orders.CustomerID = Customers.CustomerID
per_query.description: Control: UnitPrice is unqualified in a comma-join and IS sensitive, but this case is evaluated the same as the others against Operations, which lacks it -- included to keep the positive-case count honest rather than cherry-picked.
